decisions.thought: Plan: Incineroar leads for Intimidate, Fake Out and Parting Shot. Kingambit handles their Garchomp/Lucario-type attackers with Sword Dance and Kowtow Cleave. Gholdengo covers Dragapult and Tyranitar with special pressure. Watch for Dragapult's speed and Tyranitar's Rock/Dark typing, and expect Gholdengo to be a key target.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to pick three Pokémon against a team with Garchomp, Dragapult, Gholdengo, Tyranitar, Greninja, and Lucario, weighing which of my own options like Incineroar can best handle their speed and coverage.

I'll settle on Incineroar as the lead for intimidate and utility, with Gholdengo for special power and Kingambit as a solid answer to their physical threats, keeping the lineup simple rather than overthinking Garchomp or Corviknight alternatives.

Plan: Incineroar leads with Fake Out to flinch Garchomp (already at Atk -1 from Intimidate). Then pressure with Darkest Lariat or Flare Blitz, using Parting Shot to switch into Gholdengo or Kingambit when needed. Opponent so far: Garchomp (Sand Veil or Rough Skin). Still unseen: Dragapult (fast, possibly Infiltrator), Tyranitar, Greninja, Lucario, Gholdengo. Kingambit's Sword Dance is good once Garchomp is gone or weakened.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: For turn 1, Fake Out looks strong since it has priority over the slower Incineroar, flinching Garchomp and dropping its attack before it can act. I'm also weighing Darkest Lariat as an alternative option.

decisions.thought: 58% MOVE: earthquake, 15% MOVE: stealthrock, 11% MOVE: swordsdance

Garchomp (Rough Skin, possibly Sand Veil) is at 86% and -1 Atk from Intimidate. Our Incineroar is at 177/202 with Sitrus Berry. Garchomp likely outspeeds us. Darkest Lariat is neutral and hits hard. Gholdengo's Thunderbolt is useless here because Ground is immune to Electric. Kingambit is weak to Ground, so keep it out until Garchomp is gone. Watch for Dragapult (fast) and Tyranitar. Keep Gholdengo for special pressure later.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Checking the matchup: Garchomp sits at 86% HP with an Attack drop, while Incineroar is at 177/202. Neither of Incineroar's moves hits hard here since Dark is neutral against Dragon/Ground and Flare Blitz is quarter-effective, so Garchomp isn't in immediate danger from damage alone.

Looking at other threats, Kingambit's Dark and Steel moves are also neutral or unhelpful against Garchomp, and Gholdengo's Thunderbolt would simply whiff since Ground is immune to Electric. Darkest Lariat at 85 BP neutral seems like the most reasonable option right now, ignoring Garchomp's stat changes when calculating damage.

decisions.thought: Incineroar fainted to Earthquake from a Life Orb Garchomp (Rough Skin, Atk -1 from Intimidate, now 76%). Their known threats are Garchomp (Earthquake) and unseen Dragapult, Tyranitar, Greninja, Lucario, Gholdengo. Earthquake hits both my remaining Pokemon for 2x. Kingambit is bulkier (207 HP, 140 Def) and can take a hit. Kowtow Cleave or Iron Head should pressure Garchomp. Gholdengo is faster and can use Shadow Ball, but it is fragile to Earthquake. Watch for Dragapult's speed. Use Gholdengo later for special pressure.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Incineroar down and Garchomp at 76% packing Life Orb Earthquake, I need to pick between Gholdengo and Kingambit—but both are Steel-types that take 2x from Earthquake, so neither is a safe switch-in.

Gholdengo's Thunderbolt is dead weight here, though Shadow Ball or Make It Rain can chip Garchomp for decent damage while avoiding Rough Skin since they're special hits. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave hits harder but triggers Rough Skin on contact, and it's slower too, so Gholdengo's speed advantage to strike first seems like the better angle if Garchomp doesn't just click Earthquake.

With Supreme Overlord getting a boost from the one fainted ally, I'll go with Kingambit.

decisions.thought: 78% MOVE: earthquake, 6% SWITCH: tyranitar, 6% MOVE: swordsdance

Lost Incineroar to Earthquake from a Life Orb Garchomp, now at 76%. Kingambit (70 Spe) is slower than Garchomp, so Garchomp hits first. Garchomp's Earthquake is 2x on my Steel types, so Gholdengo is a poor switch-in. Kowtow Cleave is my strongest attack into Garchomp now. Sword Dance could come later if Kingambit survives Earthquake. Still unseen: Dragapult (very fast), Tyranitar, Greninja, Lucario, Gholdengo. Their Life Orb and Rough Skin wear down attackers that make contact.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is slower than Garchomp, and since Kingambit is Dark/Steel, Garchomp's Earthquake hits it super effectively for 2x damage despite the Atk drop from Life Orb recoil considerations.

Still, Garchomp likely only does 60-70% to Kingambit's 207 HP, not a guaranteed KO, while Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave hits neutrally for solid but non-lethal damage back. I'm weighing whether to switch to Gholdengo, but its Steel typing also makes it vulnerable to Earthquake, so that's not a great option either — Kowtow Cleave now, trading hits with Garchomp, seems like the better line.

decisions.thought: 85% MOVE: earthquake, 8% MOVE: knockoff, 5% SWITCH: dragapult

Kingambit is at 18 HP and will likely die to Tyranitar's move before it acts, since Tyranitar is probably faster. Switching to a healthy Gholdengo instead. Gholdengo outspeeds Tyranitar and Make It Rain is super effective on its Rock type. Watch out for Crunch, which is 2x on Gholdengo's Ghost side. Still unseen: Dragapult, Greninja, Lucario, and possibly Gholdengo. Dragapult is the main speed threat.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit is down to 18 HP against Tyranitar in sandstorm, likely slower, so it'll probably die regardless of what I do—I'm weighing whether Iron Head's super effective damage against the Rock typing is worth it even if the Dark typing resists it.

Alternatively, switching to Gholdengo seems safer since it's at full HP and can tank a Crunch despite the Dark weakness, though Rock moves get resisted by its Steel typing. Since Kingambit is nearly spent anyway, sacrificing it for one solid hit on Tyranitar before bringing in Gholdengo might be the better play.

Speed-wise Tyranitar almost certainly outpaces Kingambit, so switching to Gholdengo looks safer since it outspeeds Tyranitar entirely. Gholdengo can then threaten with Make It Rain for solid Steel coverage against Rock-type Tyranitar, while Shadow Ball and Thunderbolt remain roughly neutral options.

I'm weighing whether Gholdengo survives an incoming Crunch given its decent Defense, versus the fact that Kingambit at 18 HP is essentially already lost to Sand chip damage regardless. Trading Kingambit for one big hit with Iron Head might be worth it, but switching preserves Gholdengo at full health as a cleaner long-term answer.

Running the numbers, Kingambit's boosted Iron Head against Tyranitar's defense comes out to roughly 158 damage with STAB and the super-effective multiplier — a massive chunk against Tyranitar's ~190 HP.

That said, the problem is speed: Tyranitar almost certainly moves first and can KO Kingambit outright with Crunch or Stone Edge before it even attacks, making this a risky line. Switching to Gholdengo instead seems safer, letting it tank the hit and respond with Make It Rain.

Gholdengo's at 4 HP but faster than Tyranitar, so I'm checking if Make It Rain can secure the KO - it's super effective against Rock/Dark and Gholdengo's 185 SpA should hit hard against Tyranitar's SpD range.

So Make It Rain is the pick, Sand Stream aside. Tyranitar could have something like Focus Sash, but it shouldn't change the call.

decisions.thought: 86% MOVE: suckerpunch, 8% MOVE: shadowball, 4% MOVE: uturn

Kingambit (18 HP, Black Glasses, two fallen allies) is far slower than Dragapult, which will likely KO it first. Sucker Punch has +1 priority, so it hits first if Dragapult attacks. Dark is super effective on Dragapult's Ghost typing. Unknown Dragapult ability (Clear Body, Infiltrator, or Cursed Body) and item. Remaining opponent Pokemon: Greninja, Lucario, and possibly Gholdengo. Dragapult's Shadow Ball or Dragon Darts would hit hard. Gholdengo is the lone Ghost-typed threat I can't handle with Dark moves, so keep track of it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Kingambit at just 18 HP, I'm weighing whether its Dark-type Kowtow Cleave can knock out Dragapult before it gets outsped and hit back—factoring in the boosted power from Black Glasses and fainted allies against Dragapult's own offensive options like Dragon Darts and Shadow Ball.

Since Kingambit can't out-speed Dragapult, Sucker Punch is the better call since priority lets it strike first even though it won't quite KO; Kowtow Cleave hits harder but goes too slow and Dragapult would kill Kingambit before it connects. I'll go with Sucker Punch for the guaranteed first hit.
